note: Regulator, age and college rules are from the codified rules at 23 CAR Part 358. The 13% is the first tier of the net casino gaming receipts tax that covers sports wagering, stepping to 20% above $150M.

10% of adjusted gross receipts for mobile against 8% retail, capped by A.R.S. 5-1318. College props are barred; college game outcomes are allowed. Source is the Department's own signed 2025 letter, as its website is behind a challenge page.
Tax, age and the collegiate proposition-bet ban are from the Division of Gaming's rules, 1 CCR 207-2.
13.75% of gross gaming revenue under Public Act 21-23. Wagers on Connecticut college teams are barred except in permitted multi-team tournaments.

Tax is tiered by licence class under DC Code 36-621.15: 30% for Class C, the district-wide online licence, 20% for Class A (the stadium books) and 10% for Class B. Age 18, not 21. No wagering on events held in DC or on a DC college team.
The 50% is the statutory state share of net sports lottery proceeds under 29 Del. C. Ch. 48, a revenue allocation rather than a conventional tax. Delaware-based teams are excluded.

Regulation is layered: the Seminole Tribal Gaming Commission regulates under the 2021 compact, and Fla. Stat. 285.710(7) makes the FGCC the state compliance agency. No gross-revenue tax; the Tribe pays a revenue share. The 2021 compact excludes proposition bets on college sports (the compact as filed with the Interior Department, bia.gov).
Tax confirmed in Iowa Code 99F.11. Player props on athletes from Iowa colleges are prohibited; other college wagering is allowed.

Tax is graduated from 20% to 40% of adjusted gross receipts with a separate per-wager tax, so no single rate is quoted. No online wagers on Illinois college teams and none on an individual student athlete.
9.5% of adjusted gross receipts. A 2024 Commission directive limits college wagering to NCAA Division I and bars in-play college player props.
The Kansas Lottery owns and operates wagering; the Racing and Gaming Commission certifies and enforces. The 10% is a statutory revenue share rather than an excise.

regulator: Kentucky Horse Racing and Gaming Corporation
note: 14.25% online against 9.75% retail under KRS 138.552. HB 904 (2026) raised the age from 18 to 21 and barred negative-outcome props on Kentucky college athletes.
La. R.S. 27:625 levies 21.5% on net proceeds wagered electronically against 10% onsite. No prop bet on an individual athlete in any college event, in-state or not.
20% of gross revenue online against 15% retail under MGL c.23N s.14. 205 CMR 247.01 bars all college player props and any Massachusetts college team outside a tournament.

regulator: Maryland Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
note: The mobile rate rose to 20% on 1 July 2025; retail is taxed at 15%. Player props on college athletes stopped on 1 March 2024 by Commission directive (a 2026 bill to put that in law did not pass the Senate).

regulator: Gambling Control Unit, Maine Department of Public Safety
note: Maine bars wagering on any event a Maine college team plays in (8 MRS 1202(11)).
8.4% on adjusted gross receipts (MCL 432.414(1)), retail and online alike. A city may add a 1.25% municipal services fee.
Mo. Const. art. III s.39(g) bars props on an individual athlete in a college game involving an in-state team; college game bets are allowed.
No state-licensed retail sportsbooks; tribal casino sportsbooks sit outside the Commission's jurisdiction.

regulator: New Jersey Division of Gaming Enforcement
note: 19.75% is the online rate, raised on 1 July 2025 by P.L.2025 c.66. Retail is taxed separately at a lower rate. No bets on New Jersey college teams anywhere, or on college events held in New Jersey (the Division's approved events list).

6.75% is the top tier of a graduated fee on gross gaming revenue. Age 21 (NRS 463.350). You can open a mobile sports account remotely, but cannot bet on it until you show photo ID in person at the book or an affiliated location (Commission Regulations 5.225(7) and 22.140(6)). College events are permitted wagers (Regulation 22).

No wagers on events involving any New York college team, wherever played, or on high school events. The 51% rate on gross gaming revenue is set in the licence awards; the State Comptroller states it (osc.ny.gov, October 2023) and reports $1.3 billion collected in fiscal 2026 (September 2026).

Verified against the Ohio Revised Code: 20% of sports gaming receipts (5753.021), regulator in 3775.01, age 21 in 3775.12. No individual-athlete props on NCAA events (the Commission's approved wagering catalogue).
A lottery-run single-vendor model, so there is no gross-revenue tax rate. Separate tribal retail sportsbooks operate under compacts.
34% to the state on daily gross sports wagering revenue, plus a 2% local share kept for public-interest grants (36% in all), per the Gaming Control Board's own FAQ.

Tennessee taxes handle rather than revenue, at 1.85% of gross handle. Online only: the regulator states physical sportsbooks and kiosks are not legal. No individual player props in college events (Council rule 1350-01).
15% of adjusted gross revenue. No wagers on Virginia college teams, and college player props are banned outright.
Tax and the age-21 requirement are quoted from WV Code 29-22D-16 and 29-22D-15.
Online only, no retail sportsbooks. 10% of online sports wagering revenue is remitted to the state (W.S. 9-24-104(a)) and the minimum age is 18 (W.S. 9-24-105).
